definition: A symbolic reasoning system that applies geometric inference rules to derive new facts from given premises using forward chaining.
assumptions: Geometric facts can be represented as predicates with arguments
Inference rules can be expressed as if-then statements
Forward chaining can derive all logically necessary conclusions
The problem format can be parsed into structured representations
invariants: Only valid geometric inference rules are applied
Facts are only added if not already present
The system terminates after maximum iterations or no new facts
non_negotiable_steps: Check if conclusion is in derived facts
deviations: Simplified representation compared to full geometric algebra
Limited set of inference rules (15 vs hundreds in complete systems)
limitations: Cannot solve IMO-level problems (0% success rate)
